title: wg: targeted-messages-01 L453 Under RFC 9420, a leaf HPKE key is not tied to an epoch
description:
draft-ietf-mls-targeted-messages (targeted-messages-01), 8.4 Forward Secrecy. Editors' copy mlswg/mls-targeted-messages at ae3ab52, L453.

Text: "Compromising the recipient's leaf private key therefore exposes all targeted messages encrypted to that key within the epoch. Forward secrecy is at epoch
granularity only: it depends on the key schedule advancing to a new epoch and on
the recipient deleting the previous epoch's leaf private key. Applications that
require stronger forward secrecy guarantees SHOULD advance the epoch frequently."

Problem: Under RFC 9420, a leaf HPKE key is not tied to an epoch. It changes only when the recipient's own leaf is updated, by its own Update/Commit or a path covering it, so there is no "previous epoch's leaf private key" to delete when others commit. Advancing the epoch does not refresh the recipient's leaf key, and decryption needs both the leaf key and the epoch's exporter-derived PSK. Published -01 has the same text.

Suggested fix: State that decryption needs both the recipient's leaf HPKE private key and that epoch's targeted_message_psk. State that forward secrecy depends on deleting old exporter-derived secrets and on the recipient rotating its own leaf key. Replace "advance the epoch frequently" with a SHOULD that recipients update their own leaf node regularly.

Severity: medium. Verifier: narrow (The core is sound: under RFC 9420, a leaf HPKE key changes only when that member's own leaf is updated, so "deleting the previous epoch's leaf private key" and "advance the epoch frequently" do not describe how to get forward secrecy. The claim that line 453 contradicts lines 403-404 is weaker, because in practice a compromised device also holds the exporter secret. The rewrite therefore drops the contradiction argument.)
